content.text:
Here's the fuller picture on `0dd2857`:

**What the hook does**: `use-legacy-profile-sync-migration.ts` runs once at startup to migrate old localStorage-based git sync settings (from before the backend owned per-profile settings) into the new backend-managed `.type/settings.json` / device-local git config. It reads a legacy blob, calls `updateAppConfig` + `updateProfileSettings` per profile, and is meant to run exactly once.

**The bug**: the effect's guard clause was just `if (!profilesSnapshot || profilesBusy) return;` — no "already migrated" flag. Since `profilesSnapshot` and `profilesBusy` both change on **every settings save** (any save cycles busy state), the effect would fire again after the user saved fresh git sync settings, re-read the stale legacy localStorage blob, and silently overwrite what the user just typed in — e.g. you set a new git remote URL, save, and it reverts back to old settings a moment later with no error shown.

**The fix**: adds a `useRef` flag set to `true` synchronously (before any `await`) so the migration can run at most once per app session, and can't race itself if a re-render fires mid-migration.

This bug is still present on `feat/react-native-monorepo`'s copy of the file (confirmed above — no guard there), so it's worth porting forward regardless of the release.
